topStories.headline: Storm Swamps the Embarcadero: Waves Top Barriers, Roads Close as Atmospheric River Hits SF
topStories.dek: A powerful atmospheric river on November 18 sent bay water over flood barriers near Pier 14, flooding sidewalks, bike lanes, and one traffic lane along the Embarcadero.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's waterfront took a direct hit on Wednesday, November 18, when a powerful atmospheric river storm drove bay waves over flood barriers near Pier 14, inundating stretches of the Embarcadero with water that reached sidewalks, bike lanes, and at least one vehicle travel lane. The surge reduced that section of the roadway to a single lane and contributed to significant traffic backups through the Financial District.

The city recorded 2.28 inches of rain by 3 p.m. on November 18 — the most rainfall on that calendar date since 1918, according to the National Weather Service, and nearly matching San Francisco's entire average November total of 2.6 inches. Storm waves just off the immediate coast reached 16.4 feet.

The flooding triggered ferry cancellations on bay routes and dozens of flight cancellations at SFO, where a full ground stop was in place until noon. San Francisco Public Works responded to reports of downed trees across the city, while Caltrans closed multiple freeway ramps on I-280 and Highway 101 due to standing water. Waymo autonomous vehicles stalled in flooded streets, disrupting robo-taxi service throughout the day; the company said service resumed on November 19.

The Embarcadero's vulnerability had been flagged just days before the storm. An Axios report published November 9 noted that unusually high October tides had already overtopped the waterfront near Pier 14 during calm weather, and that the Port of San Francisco was preparing temporary flood barriers at four locations while longer-term coastal resilience projects move through planning. City officials have warned that without action, 100 to 500 structures along the waterfront could face flood risk by 2050.

topStories.headline: The Tree Is Up: Union Square's Real Fir Arrives for the First Time in 16 Years
topStories.dek: Workers hauled a live Christmas tree across the Bay Bridge and hoisted it into place at Union Square on November 19, with lighting expected by Black Friday.
topStories.body:
The return of a real Christmas tree to Union Square moved from announcement to reality on Thursday, November 19, when maintenance crews lifted the live fir into place at the center of the plaza. Workers had trucked the tree across the Bay Bridge and into downtown San Francisco before raising it in front of the cameras of several local news crews who documented the moment.

It is the first real tree to stand in Union Square since 2010. For the past 15-plus years the plaza relied on an artificial tree sponsored by Macy's; after the retailer ended its decades-long sponsorship of the holiday centerpiece this year, the city stepped in and paid for a fresh-cut tree instead. The Union Square Alliance, which manages programming for the plaza, says lighting is expected to happen by Black Friday, November 27, though no precise lighting ceremony time had been announced as of this week.

Marisa Rodriguez, CEO of the Union Square Alliance, told KGO-TV that the square is "the Rockefeller Center of the West." City officials note the plaza historically draws more than one million visitors during the winter holiday season. Other seasonal staples continue alongside the new tree: Macy's window displays and the SF SPCA's annual holiday showcase are both expected to return.

topStories.headline: Banksy Limitless Opens December 4 in Former H&M Space on Powell Street
topStories.dek: A 25,000-square-foot immersive exhibition of more than 250 works attributed to the street artist Banksy will open at 150 Powell Street on December 4, filling one of Union Square's largest vacant storefronts.
topStories.body:
One of Union Square's most prominent empty storefronts — the former H&M flagship at 150 Powell Street — will come back to life on December 4, when Banksy Limitless opens its doors for what organizers describe as a 75-minute immersive experience spanning 25,000 square feet. The exhibit features more than 250 pieces ranging from certified originals and photographs to large-scale installations, including murals that were physically removed from their original urban surfaces and professionally restored.

The show has previously had reportedly sold-out runs in London and Sydney before coming to San Francisco. Tickets are priced at $35. Organizers have not announced a closing date, describing the run as lasting through the spring. The exhibition is not authorized or endorsed by Banksy, who famously disavows commercial exhibitions of his work.

The arrival of Banksy Limitless is one of several recent moves to activate Union Square's empty anchor spaces with temporary uses. The former Saks Fifth Avenue building at 384 Post Street has been wrapped in a large interactive mural by its owner, Lincoln Property Co. and Cara Investment. Meanwhile, SFMade opened its first permanent retail storefront in the neighborhood earlier this month, and the Safeway Holiday Ice Rink is already in its 19th season in the plaza. Property sources cited by the SF Chronicle say a permanent retailer is expected to follow the Banksy exhibit at 150 Powell once the show wraps.

moreNews.headline: Embarcadero Park Pavilion Design Heads to Review as Groundbreaking Approaches
moreNews.body: The $40 million overhaul of Embarcadero Plaza and Sue Bierman Park is moving deeper into detailed design. In mid-October 2026, two pavilion concept options — including variations on a structure described as roughly 85 feet long and 40 feet tall — went to design review for the planned 5-acre waterfront park at the foot of Market Street. The Recreation and Park Commission unanimously approved the final concept design in June 2026; the project, a public-private partnership with BXP (owner of Embarcadero Center), Crankstart, and other philanthropic donors, is expected to break ground in late 2026 or 2027. The finished park would replace the existing concrete plaza with lawns, gardens, walking paths, and a large flexible event lawn.

moreNews.headline: Embarcadero Center Marks 40 Years of Holiday Lighting
moreNews.body: On Wednesday, November 18, Embarcadero Center held its 40th Annual Holiday Lighting Ceremony and Holiday Market, a free event held from 4 to 6 p.m. at the Sacramento and Front Street complex in the Financial District. The ceremony — which this year coincided with the season's first major atmospheric river storm — is an annual kickoff to the holiday season at the waterfront office and retail complex.

restaurants.name: Sisterita

restaurants.name: John's Grill

restaurants.name: HINODEYA Ramen Union Square

restaurants.name: Nopa Fish

restaurants.name: Parachute Bakery

restaurants.name: Roli Roti Gourmet Rotisserie

hotels.name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco

hotels.name: Palace Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel
hotels.description: San Francisco landmark since 1909, with a sky-lit indoor pool, 556 rooms, and two iconic dining venues—the crystal-chandeliered Garden Court and the celebrated Pied Piper Bar.

hotels.name: Grand Hyatt San Francisco Union Square
hotels.description: Situated directly on Union Square, this flagship hotel offers panoramic city views, easy cable car access, and proximity to Chinatown and the Financial District.

hotels.name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District

hotels.name: Handlery Union Square Hotel

hotels.name: Beacon Grand, A Union Square Hotel

hotels.name: Chancellor Hotel on Union Square
